scenario.brief: A small startup is preparing to launch its first public website.
scenario.workload: The website contains HTML, CSS, JavaScript and images only.
requirements: The website origin should not be directly exposed to the public

questions.title: Choose the Origin
questions.question: The website contains only static files. The customer wants a low-cost solution with the least operational overhead. Which approach best meets these requirements?

options.text: Run the website on a dedicated EC2 instance
Store the website files in Amazon S3
Run the website on an EC2 Auto Scaling group
Store the website files in Amazon EBS

questions.wrong_hint: Focus on the words static files and least operational overhead. Does this workload really require a server?
questions.clue: Your origin does not need a running server. Think object storage.

questions.title: Reach Global Users
questions.question: The startup expects users from multiple countries and wants fast content delivery without managing additional servers. Which AWS service should be placed in front of the website origin?
questions.wrong_hint: Look for a service designed to cache and deliver content through globally distributed edge locations.
questions.clue: Bring content closer to users through a global content delivery network.

questions.title: Secure the Connection
questions.question: The customer requires visitors to access the website using HTTPS. Which AWS service can provide and manage the required TLS certificate?
questions.wrong_hint: The requirement is specifically about a managed TLS certificate for HTTPS.
questions.clue: The architecture needs an AWS-managed certificate attached at the HTTPS entry point.

questions.title: Connect the Domain
questions.question: The company wants customers to reach the website using its own domain name. Which AWS service is designed to manage DNS records and route the domain to AWS resources?
questions.wrong_hint: Think about DNS rather than networking, infrastructure deployment or threat detection.
questions.clue: The custom domain needs a DNS service that can direct users toward the application.

questions.title: Protect the Origin
questions.question: The customer wants users to access the website through CloudFront, but does not want the S3 origin directly exposed to the public. Which design best satisfies this requirement?

options.text: Make the S3 bucket public and rely on a difficult bucket name
Keep the S3 bucket private and allow CloudFront controlled access to the origin
Allow public read access to every object
Move the static files to an EC2 instance with a public IP address

questions.wrong_hint: The requirement says the origin itself must not be publicly accessible. CloudFront still needs permission to retrieve the objects.
questions.clue: Keep the origin private and establish controlled access between the distribution and the origin.
